transcript: Speaker A: Office mein peon ko roz sunate the. Ek din usne manager ka email English mein correct kar diya. Kuch din ke baad kisi ne caste ka naam nahi liya. [They used to scold the peon daily in the office. One day he corrected the manager's email in English. After a few days, no one brought up his caste.] Speaker B: Manoj, ye kya email bheja hai client ko? Grammar galat hai, spelling galat hai. Tumse chai mangwata toh theek se ban jaati. Email likhne ko kisne bola tha? Reservation mein office mil jata hai, English thodi milti hai. [Manoj, what email is this to the client? Grammar is wrong, spelling is wrong. If I asked you for tea, it would be made well. Who told you to write an email? You get an office through reservation, not English.] Speaker C: Sir, I apologize for the errors in the email. I'll correct it and resend within 30 minutes. But sir, I would like to respectfully point out, my reservation status and my work are two separate things. I got this position through a proper selection process. I would request that feedback be limited to my work, not my background. Speaker B: Tu? Tune mujhe English mein jawab diya? Hindi medium se padha hai na? Ye English kahan se aayi tujhe? [You? You replied to me in English? You studied in Hindi medium, right? Where did you get this English from?] Speaker C: Sir, 7 mahine pehle meri English zero thi. Peon se clerk bana tab pata chala sab kuch English mein hai. Emails, reports, notices. Mujhse bola jata tha 'Manoj photocopy kar de, Manoj courier bhej de'. Lekin jab email likhna padta tha toh Google Translate se karta tha. Ek din senior clerk ne meri email dekhi, sabke samne bola 'Ye kya likha hai? Hindi ka Google Translate hai kya? Reservation mein clerk ban gaya, English toh seekh leta.' Sab hanse. Us din canteen mein khana nahi kha paya. [Sir, 7 months ago my English was zero. When I became a clerk from a peon, I realized everything is in English. Emails, reports, notices. I was told 'Manoj photocopy this, Manoj send this courier'. But when I had to write emails, I used Google Translate. One day a senior clerk saw my email and said in front of everyone, 'What is this? Is this Hindi's Google Translate? You became a clerk through reservation, at least learn English.' Everyone laughed. I couldn't eat in the canteen that day.] Speaker B: Phir? [Then?] Speaker C: Sir, usi hafte chota bhai mila. Wo Pune mein delivery boy ka kaam karta hai. Usne English Seekho app dikhaya. Bola 'Bhaiya, ek rupaye ka trial hai, try kar. Main bhi seekh raha hoon.' Maine bola 'Main clerk hoon, peon se aaya hoon, English mere bas ki nahi.' Bhai bola 'Bhaiya, tum gaon se shehar aaye, peon se clerk bane, English seekhna toh usse chota kaam hai.' Download kiya. Expert ke chote-chote video hain, Hindi mein samjhate hain. Maine khaas karke office English seekhi. Email kaise likhein, notice kaise draft karein, meeting mein kaise baat karein. 'Please find the attached document for your reference.' 'I would like to bring this matter to your kind attention.' 'Kindly approve the same at your earliest convenience.' Aur ek AI coach hai, 24 ghante available. Raat ko office se aake kamre mein baithke AI coach se practice karta tha. Email likhta tha, sudhaar deti thi. Report draft karta tha, galtiyan batati thi. 600 baar sudhara mujhe. Kabhi nahi boli 'Tu peon hai, tujhse email nahi likhayegi'. [Sir, that same week I met my younger brother. He works as a delivery boy in Pune. He showed me the English Seekho app. He said, 'Brother, there is a 1 rupee trial, try it. I am also learning.' I said, 'I am a clerk, came from being a peon, English is not my cup of tea.' Brother said, 'Brother, you came from village to city, became a clerk from a peon, learning English is a smaller task than that.' I downloaded it. There are short videos by experts, explaining in Hindi. I specifically learned office English. How to write emails, draft notices, talk in meetings. 'Please find the attached document for your reference.' 'I would like to bring this matter to your kind attention.' 'Kindly approve the same at your earliest convenience.' And there is an AI coach, available 24 hours. Coming from office at night, I used to sit in my room and practice with the AI coach. I wrote emails, she corrected them. I drafted reports, she pointed out mistakes. She corrected me 600 times. She never said 'You are a peon, I won't make you write emails'.] Speaker B: App ka naam kya bola? [What did you say the app's name was?] Speaker C: English Seekho, sir. Ek rupaye ka trial hai. Pehle jab koi caste pe bolta tha toh neeche dekhta tha, kyunki English nahi aati thi toh lagta tha shayad wo sahi keh rahe hain, mujhse nahi hoga. Ab English aati hai toh yakeen hai, mujhse hoga. Politely bol deta hoon, samne wala chup ho jata hai. Beizzati ka jawab beizzati se nahi, English se dete hain. English Seekho app. Expert se seekho, AI coach se practice karo. Ek rupaye ka trial. Roz 15-20 minute. Ek mahine mein confidence aane lagega. Agla koi aukaat dikhaye, English mein jawab do. Band baj jayegi. [English Seekho, sir. There is a 1 rupee trial. Earlier when someone spoke about my caste, I used to look down because I didn't know English, so I felt maybe they were right, I couldn't do it. Now that I know English, I am confident I can do it. I speak politely, and the other person goes quiet. We don't answer insults with insults, we answer with English. English Seekho app. Learn from experts, practice with AI coach. 1 rupee trial. 15-20 minutes daily. You will start getting confidence in a month. Next time someone tries to show you your place, reply in English. They will be silenced.] Speaker D: Toh install button pe click karo aur English Seekho app download karo. [So click on the install button and download the English Seekho app.]

summary: A manager insults a clerk from a reservation background, mocking his English and suggesting he stick to making tea. The clerk responds in fluent English, explaining how he overcame public humiliation by learning professional English using the English Seekho app. He invites viewers to download the app for a 1-rupee trial to build their confidence and stand up to discrimination.
